help_modal.ally_betray: Betray your ally, ending the alliance, halting trade, and weakening your defense. Trading between you is paused for 5 minutes (or until you become allies again) and others may stop trading too. And unless the other player was a traitor themselves, you'll be marked a traitor for 30 seconds. During this time an icon will be above your name and you will have a 50% defense debuff. Tribes are less likely to ally with you and players will think twice before doing so.
help_modal.ally_donate: Donate some of your troops to your ally. Used when they're low on troops and are being attacked, or when they need that extra power to crush an enemy.
help_modal.ally_donate_gold: Donate some of your gold to your ally. Used when they're low on gold and need it for buildings, or when your team member is saving for that MIRV.
help_modal.build_atom_desc: Small explosive bomb that destroys territory, buildings, ships and boats. Spawns from the nearest Missile Silo and lands in the area you first clicked to build it.
help_modal.build_city_desc: Increases your max population. Useful when you can't expand your territory or you're about to hit your population limit.
help_modal.build_defense_desc: Increases defenses around nearby borders, which show a checkered pattern. Attacks from enemies are slower and have more casualties.
help_modal.build_factory_desc: Automatically builds railroads to nearby cities, ports and other factories, and can also link up with friendly neighbors. Trains spawn regularly and give you a fixed amount of gold for each building they visit along the route, with extra gold for visiting your neighbors' buildings.
help_modal.build_hydrogen_desc: Large explosive bomb. Spawns from the nearest Missile Silo and lands in the area you first clicked to build it.
help_modal.build_menu_desc: Build these or see how many of each you already build:
help_modal.build_mirv_desc: The most powerful bomb in the game. Splits up into smaller bombs that will cover a huge range of territory. Only damages the player that you first clicked on to build it. Spawns from the nearest Missile Silo and lands in the area you first clicked to build it.
help_modal.build_port_desc: Can only be built near water. Allows building Warships. Automatically sends trade ships between ports of your country and other countries (except when trade is stopped), giving gold to both sides. Trade with a player stops automatically when you attack or are attacked by a player. It resumes after 5 minutes or if you become allies. You can manually toggle trading with "Stop trading" or "Start trading".
help_modal.build_sam_desc: Can intercept enemy missiles in its 100 pixel range. The SAM has a 7.5 second cooldown.
help_modal.build_warship_desc: Patrols in an area, capturing enemy trade ships and destroying their Boats (transport ships) and Warships. Spawns from the nearest Port and patrols the area you first clicked to build it. You can control Warships by attack-clicking on them (see action Attack under Hotkeys) and then attack-clicking the new area you want them to move to. Warships can level up (max level 3) by capturing enemy trade ships and destroying their transport boats and Warships. Leveling up increases the Warship's damage and health.
help_modal.exit_confirmation: Are you sure you want to exit the game?
help_modal.icon_ally: Handshake - Ally. This player is your ally.
help_modal.icon_crown: Crown - Number 1. This is the top player in the leaderboard.
help_modal.icon_desc: Examples of some of the ingame icons you will encounter and what they mean:
help_modal.icon_embargo: Dollar stop sign - Embargo. This player has stopped trading with you automatically or manually.
help_modal.icon_request: Envelope - Alliance request. This player has sent you an alliance request.
help_modal.icon_traitor: Broken shield - Traitor. This player attacked an ally.
help_modal.in_game_tutorial_desc: Learn by playing: a solo game with a step-by-step guide that walks you through spawning, attacking, building and nukes.
help_modal.info_alliance: Send an alliance request to the player. Allies can share resources and troops, but can't attack each other.
help_modal.info_ally_desc: When you ally with a player, the following new icons become available:
help_modal.info_chat: Send a quick chat message to the player. Select a Category, a Phrase, and if the phrase contains [P1] select a Player name to replace it with. Hit Send.
help_modal.info_emoji: Send an emoji to the player.
help_modal.info_enemy_desc: Contains information such as the selected player's name, gold, troops, stopped trading with you, nukes sent to you, and if the player is a traitor. Stopped trading means you won't receive gold from them and they won't sent you gold via trade ships. Manually (if the player clicked "Stop trading", which lasts until you both click "Start trading") or automatically (if you betrayed your alliance, which lasts until you become allies again or after 5 minutes). Traitor displays Yes for 30 seconds when the player betrayed and attacked a player who was in an alliance with them. The icons below represent the following interactions:
help_modal.info_target: Place a target mark on the player, marking it for all allies, used to coordinate attacks.
help_modal.info_trade: Use "Stop trading" to stop giving the player gold and receiving their gold via trade ships. If you both click "Start trading" it will start again.
help_modal.option_pause: Pause/Unpause the game - Unavailable in public games.
help_modal.option_settings: Settings - Open the settings menu. Inside you can toggle things like Alternate view, Emojis, Dark Mode, Hidden names, action on left click and more.
help_modal.option_speed: Speed - Adjust the game speed. Unavailable in public games.
help_modal.option_timer: Timer - Time passed since the start of the game.
help_modal.radial_boat: Send a Boat (transport ship) to attack at the selected location. Only available if you have access to water.
help_modal.radial_desc: Right clicking (or touch on mobile) opens the Radial menu. Right click outside it to close it. From the menu you can:
help_modal.radial_donate_gold: Opens the gold donation slider menu so you can quickly send allies gold.
help_modal.radial_donate_troops: Donate troops equivalent to your attack ratio slider percentage to the ally you opened the radial menu on.
help_modal.troubleshooting_desc: If you experience performance issues, crashes, or other problems while playing, please visit our Troubleshooting page for help diagnosing and fixing common issues:
help_modal.ui_attack_ratio: Attack ratio - The amount of troops that will be used when you attack. You can adjust the attack ratio using the slider. Having more attacking troops than defending troops will make you lose fewer troops in the attack, while having less will increase the damage dealt to your attacking troops. The effect doesn't go beyond ratios of 2:1.
help_modal.ui_control_desc: The control panel contains the following elements:
help_modal.ui_events_alliance: Alliance - Alliance requests can be accepted or rejected. Allies can share resources and troops, but can't attack each other. Clicking Focus moves the view to the player who sent the request.
help_modal.ui_events_attack: Attacks - Incoming attacks and your outgoing attacks are shown. Click the message to center the view on the attack, nuke or Boat (transport ship). You can retreat troops by clicking the red X button. This will cost the lives of 25% of your attacking troops. If you retrieve a Boat attack, the boat returns to its starting point and will attack there if the land has been captured since. Nukes can't be retreated once launched.
help_modal.ui_events_desc: The Event panel displays the latest events, requests and Quick Chat messages. Some examples are:
help_modal.ui_events_quickchat: Quick Chat - You can see sent and received chat messages here. Send a message to a player by clicking the Quick Chat icon in their Info menu.
help_modal.ui_gold: Gold - The amount of gold you have and the rate at which you gain it.
help_modal.ui_leaderboard_desc: Shows the top players of the game and their names, % owned land, gold and troops. Using Show All shows all players in the game. If you don't want to see the leaderboard, click Hide.
help_modal.ui_options_desc: The following elements can be found inside:
help_modal.ui_playeroverlay_desc: When you hover over a country, the Player info overlay appears. It shows the player type (Human, Nation, or Tribe), a Nation's attitude toward you (Hostile to Friendly), defending troops, gold, and the number of Warships and buildings they have.

tutorial.complete: You're ready! Good luck out there.

step.alliance_info: Allies can't attack each other. You can break an alliance at any time — but doing so marks you as a traitor.
step.atom_info: Atom Bomb — small tactical strikes that take out structures.
step.attack_nations: Nations have cut you off from the tribes. Attack a neighboring nation instead — they're stronger than tribes, so bring plenty of troops. The nearest ones are marked with a target. Conquer them until you have {cost} gold for a City.
step.attack_ratio: The attack ratio bar sets how many of your troops are sent out with each attack. Drag the slider to adjust it.
step.attack_wilderness: The pulsing ring marks your territory. Click on the unclaimed land next to it to attack and expand.
step.buy_city: You can afford a City! Press {key} (or tap the City icon under the control panel twice: the first tap shows its card, the second starts building), then tap your territory to place it. Cities raise your max troops.
step.buy_defense_post: Now build a Defense Post: press {key}, then click your territory near a border. Attacks on the land around it are much slower and cost the enemy far more troops.
step.buy_factory: Now build a Factory: press {key}, then click your territory to place it.
step.buy_port: Next, build a Port: press {key}, then click your coastline to place it.
step.buy_silo: Finally, build a Missile Silo: press {key}, then click your territory to place it. Silos launch atom bombs, hydrogen bombs and MIRVs.
step.buy_warship: Now build a Warship: press {key}, then click open water near your port. Warships capture trade ships and protect your waters.
step.capture_tribes: Capturing tribes is a great way to earn gold — the nearest ones are marked with a target on the map. Conquer them until you have {cost} gold for a City.
step.earn_gold: Attack neighbors to steal their land, conquer them to take their gold. You need {cost} for a {unit}.
step.factory_info: Factories are connected to cities and other factories by tracks, and spawn trains that grant gold.
step.hydrogen_info: Hydrogen Bomb — large strategic strikes that weaken the enemy.
step.launch_atom: Your silo is armed! Press {key}, then click a neighbor's territory to launch an Atom Bomb.
step.mirv_info: MIRV — a massive missile attack to cripple your enemy.
step.no_coast: You have no coastline yet. Water access is very important — it lets you send boats, build ports and trade by sea. Expand your territory until it reaches the coast.
step.port_info_ships: Ports send out trade ships, which earn you gold.
step.port_info_warships: Ports can also be used to construct warships.
step.propose_alliance: Allies secure your borders. Right-click the nation marked with a target and propose an alliance.
step.sam_info: SAM Launcher — defends against nuclear strikes by shooting down incoming missiles.
step.send_boat: Boats send your troops across water. Right-click an enemy coastline across the water to open the radial menu, then select the boat.
step.silo_loading: Your Missile Silo is loading — a nuke can be launched once it's fully ready.
step.spawn: Click anywhere on the map to pick where you spawn.
step.spawn_wait: Spot picked! You can still move it until the timer runs out — the game starts then.
step.traitor_info: Traitors get a large defense debuff for 30 seconds, so be careful.
step.troop_rate: This is your troop growth rate. Growth slows down and turns orange once your troops approach half of your max.
step.troops: Keep an eye on your troop count. Attacking with too few troops leaves you weak — let them regrow between attacks.

step_touch.attack_wilderness: The pulsing ring marks your territory. Tap the unclaimed land next to it, then tap the sword in the middle of the menu to attack.

decision_desc.bgr_demand_dobruja: Ask Romania to return Southern Dobruja, lost to it in 1913.
decision_desc.deu_demand_austria: Order Vienna to hand power to the Austrian National Socialists and accept union with the Reich.
decision_desc.deu_demand_bohemia: Summon the Czech president to Berlin and demand that his state place itself under German protection.
decision_desc.deu_demand_danzig: Demand the Free City of Danzig and a German road and railway across the Polish corridor.
decision_desc.deu_demand_memel: Demand that Lithuania return the Memel Territory to the Reich, by force if need be.
decision_desc.deu_demand_sudeten: Claim the German-speaking border districts of Czechoslovakia and force the great powers to settle the question.
decision_desc.deu_invite_balkans: Invite a Balkan state to join the Tripartite Pact and stand with the Axis.
decision_desc.deu_sign_tripartite: Bind Germany, Italy and Japan to aid one another against any power that enters the war against them.
decision_desc.deu_soviet_pact_proposal: Send the foreign minister to Moscow to offer a non-aggression pact and a secret division of eastern Europe.
decision_desc.fra_dissolve_vichy: With Paris in French hands again, the Provisional Government declares the acts of the Vichy regime void and takes over the territories it still holds.
decision_desc.gbr_destroyers_for_bases: Offer the United States long leases on Atlantic bases in return for fifty old destroyers.
decision_desc.gbr_free_french_recognition: Recognise the French leaders who fight on from London as the voice of France at war.
decision_desc.gbr_guarantee_poland: Pledge to defend Poland if its independence is threatened, and ask France to join.
decision_desc.gbr_guarantee_romania_greece: Extend the same pledge of defence to Romania and Greece to hold the eastern Mediterranean.
decision_desc.gbr_levant_intervention: Prepare an advance from Palestine into Vichy-held Syria and Lebanon.
decision_desc.gbr_occupy_iceland: With Denmark in German hands, land troops in Iceland before Germany can use it against the Atlantic routes.
decision_desc.gen_annex_subject: Over 180 days, merge a fully integrated puppet and its army into our own state.
decision_desc.gen_coup_com: For 90 days, arms and money go to communists abroad; if they reach half the country's support, its government falls.
decision_desc.gen_coup_dem: For 90 days, arms and money go to democrats abroad; if they reach half the country's support, its government falls.
decision_desc.gen_coup_fas: For 90 days, arms and money go to fascists abroad; if they reach half the country's support, its government falls.
decision_desc.gen_coup_neu: For 90 days, arms and money go to non-aligned factions abroad; if they reach half the country's support, its government falls.
decision_desc.gen_demand_autonomy: Push our overlord for a larger say in our own affairs: autonomy +10%.
decision_desc.gen_downgrade_subject: Bring a subject with no autonomy left one step closer under our rule.
decision_desc.gen_emergency_draft: Wider age limits and fewer deferments put more men into uniform at once.
decision_desc.gen_exile_recruit: Enlist our citizens who escaped abroad and those in allied hands: manpower from 1% of the core population our side holds.
decision_desc.gen_exile_resistance: Send money, radios and organisers into our occupied homeland: resistance there grows faster for 90 days.
decision_desc.gen_fortify_border: Positions and obstacles go up quickly along the border with the most threatening neighbour.
decision_desc.gen_hire_general: An able colonel is promoted to general and given an army to lead.
decision_desc.gen_industrial_subsidy: Grants to builders and manufacturers speed up work on civilian factories.
decision_desc.gen_invite_neighbours: Invite a non-aligned neighbour without a faction into the entente we lead.
decision_desc.gen_join_allies: Ask the leader of the Allies to accept us as a member.
decision_desc.gen_join_axis: Ask the leader of the Axis to accept us as a member.
decision_desc.gen_join_comintern: Ask the leader of the Comintern to accept us as a member.
decision_desc.gen_martial_law: The army takes over policing and bans gatherings; order returns, but the factories slow down.
decision_desc.gen_partisan_support: Supply the partisans behind enemy lines in our occupied lands: resistance there rises for 90 days.
decision_desc.gen_party_support_com: Money and leaflets for another country's communists widen their support for 180 days.
decision_desc.gen_party_support_dem: Money and newspapers for another country's democratic parties widen their support for 180 days.
decision_desc.gen_party_support_fas: Money and leaflets for another country's fascists widen their support for 180 days.
decision_desc.gen_party_support_neu: Money and newspapers for another country's non-aligned factions widen their support for 180 days.
decision_desc.gen_rally: Rallies across the country win new supporters for the ruling party for 90 days.
decision_desc.gen_release_subject: End our protection over a subject; it stays in our faction.
decision_desc.gen_request_autonomy: Our autonomy has reached its limit: ask the overlord to raise our status, or to let us go if we are already a dominion.
decision_desc.gen_restore_country: Where we have freed the core lands of a country that no longer exists, recreate its state and invite it to our faction.
decision_desc.gen_suppress_opposition: The largest opposition's papers and meetings are restricted; its support falls, but resentment grows.
decision_desc.gen_suspend_elections: General elections wait until the war is over, and the sitting parliament carries on.
decision_desc.gen_tech_exchange: Engineers sent to our faction's leader bring home a technology we still lack.
decision_desc.gen_tighten_control: For 90 days, officials and advisers sent to a subject hold back its autonomy.
decision_desc.gen_war_bonds: Selling bonds to the public raises money for the war and ties citizens to its outcome.
decision_desc.hun_request_arbitration: Ask Germany and Italy to arbitrate Hungary's claim to southern Slovakia.
decision_desc.hun_request_transylvania: Ask Berlin to settle Hungary's claim to northern Transylvania by arbitration.
decision_desc.ita_send_ctv: Four divisions of the Corpo Truppe Volontarie sail for Spain to fight beside Franco's Nationalists.
decision_desc.jpn_demand_indochina_access: Demand that the authorities of French Indochina let Japanese troops in — first the north, then the south.
decision_desc.pol_zaolzie_ultimatum: Demand the Teschen district of Silesia from Czechoslovakia while Prague is at its weakest.
decision_desc.sun_aid_spain: Ship rifles and guns to the Spanish Republic, paid for with its gold reserves.
decision_desc.sun_baltic_bases: Demand a mutual assistance pact with Soviet garrisons and bases on Baltic soil.
decision_desc.sun_baltic_ultimatum: Demand a new government and the free entry of Soviet troops, ending the state's independence.
decision_desc.sun_demand_bessarabia: Demand that Romania hand over Bessarabia and northern Bukovina within days.
decision_desc.sun_demand_karelia: Demand that Finland move its border away from Leningrad and lease Hanko as a naval base.
decision_desc.sun_offer_finnish_peace: Offer to end the war in return for the Karelian Isthmus, the Ladoga shore and land in the north.
decision_desc.sun_propose_pact: Offer Germany a non-aggression pact before the Western powers can draw us into their war.
decision_desc.tur_hatay_question: Press France to let the Sanjak of Alexandretta join Turkey.
decision_desc.usa_oil_embargo: Japanese assets in the United States are frozen and oil exports stop. Japan loses most of its fuel imports.
decision_desc.usa_recognize_exiles: Washington formally recognises the allied governments in exile and receives their envoys, backing their claim to speak for their peoples.
decision_desc.usa_volunteer_air_group: American pilots leave the services and sign on to fly fighters for China, in aircraft bought on American credit.

event_desc.aut_berlin_ultimatum: Berlin demands that the Chancellor call off his plebiscite on independence and hand power to the Austrian National Socialists, or German troops will cross the border. No foreign government has promised to help Vienna.
event_desc.bal_mutual_assistance: Moscow demands a mutual assistance pact that would station Soviet garrisons, air bases and naval bases on our soil. Germany, now bound to the Soviet Union, offers no help, and the Red Army is massing at the border. Refusing means risking war.
event_desc.bal_soviet_ultimatum: Moscow accuses us of plotting against the Soviet Union and demands a new government and free entry for any number of Soviet troops, with only hours to answer. No power in Europe is in a position to stand with us.
event_desc.bgr_fatherland_front: The Soviet Union has declared war on us and its troops are crossing the Danube. In Sofia, the Fatherland Front coalition has taken over the ministries overnight and offers to join the war against Germany.
event_desc.bgr_greek_thrace: Our army has followed the German advance into eastern Macedonia and Western Thrace, and the Greek government has gone into exile. Sofia regards the region, with its outlet to the Aegean, as land lost in 1919 and wants to join it to the kingdom.
event_desc.can_parliament_decides: Prime Minister Mackenzie King promised that Parliament would decide whether Canada goes to war. In a special session the members vote to stand with Britain, and Canada declares war on Germany in its own name, a week after Britain.
event_desc.casablanca_conference: The President and the Prime Minister have met in Casablanca to plan the coming year of the war. Before they part, they agree to accept nothing short of the unconditional surrender of Germany, Italy and Japan.
event_desc.chn_soviet_treaty: Moscow offers China a treaty of non-aggression, and with it credits, aircraft and volunteer pilots for the war against Japan. Signing will alarm Tokyo and the Western powers, but no one else is offering guns.
event_desc.chn_xian_incident: Marshal Zhang Xueliang has detained Chiang Kai-shek at Xi'an, demanding an end to the war on the Communists and a united front against Japan. Chiang's release now depends on what Nanjing is willing to promise. In Nanjing, some call for troops to march on Xi'an.
event_desc.csk_munich_dictate: The terms have reached Prague: the German-speaking border districts must be handed to Germany within days, with the fortifications built to defend them. If we refuse, we will have to fight Germany alone. None of Prague's allies will step in.
event_desc.csk_prague_ultimatum: The President has been summoned to Berlin and told that German troops will march at dawn. If he signs, Bohemia and Moravia become a German protectorate and the rest of the state falls apart; if he refuses, Prague will be bombed.
event_desc.csk_vienna_award_notice: Meeting in Vienna, the German and Italian foreign ministers have drawn a new frontier between Czechoslovakia and Hungary. The southern strip of Slovakia, with Košice, passes to Hungary; Prague was not asked to agree. There is no way to refuse.
event_desc.csk_zaolzie_ultimatum: Poland demands the Teschen district of Silesia, with its coal mines and ironworks, and gives Prague less than a day to answer. With the Sudeten frontier already gone, the army is in no position to fight on a second front. Hungary is pressing claims on the southern frontier too.
event_desc.deu_annex_west_poland: The Polish government has fled abroad and fights on from exile. Our administrators propose to join the western provinces, the corridor, Posen and eastern Upper Silesia, to the Reich by decree rather than wait for a peace treaty.
event_desc.deu_army_command: War Minister Blomberg has resigned, and the army's commander-in-chief Fritsch has been pushed out as well. Hitler means to abolish the War Ministry and command the armed forces directly through a newly created High Command of the Armed Forces. Among the generals there is talk that the army's independence is over.
event_desc.deu_austria_refused: The Austrian government has rejected the demand for union and vowed to defend its independence by plebiscite. Troops are already massed at the border. Sending them in means war; backing down shakes the regime's prestige.
event_desc.deu_case_anton: With the Allies in North Africa, Berlin no longer trusts the armistice. German columns cross the demarcation line towards the Mediterranean coast and Italian troops land on Corsica. The French State keeps its ministers but loses its last unoccupied territory.
event_desc.deu_compiegne_armistice: In the railway carriage where Germany signed the armistice of 1918, French envoys accept German terms. The north and the Atlantic coast stay occupied, a French government keeps the south and the empire, and the fleet is to be disarmed in its home ports.
event_desc.deu_croatian_state: Yugoslavia has collapsed, and its king and government have fled abroad. In Zagreb a nationalist movement has proclaimed an independent Croatian state and asks for our recognition. It would take in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Italy expects its share of the coast.
event_desc.deu_denmark_takeover: Strikes and sabotage have spread through Danish towns, and the government in Copenhagen has refused our demand for emergency measures. Our plenipotentiary proposes to end the policy of cooperation, disarm the Danish forces and rule the country directly.
event_desc.deu_hungary_coup: The Hungarian Regent has broadcast an armistice. Our troops in Budapest and the Hungarian officers who reject it can take the castle hill, make the Regent step down and hand power to a government that will keep Hungary in the war.
event_desc.deu_italy_betrayal: Rome has announced an armistice with the Allies behind our backs. Our divisions in Italy are ordered to disarm the Italian army, take the Alpine passes and the northern cities, and hold the peninsula as far south as they can.
event_desc.deu_july_plot: A bomb has gone off during a briefing at Hitler's headquarters in East Prussia. In Berlin, officers are using the reserve army's mobilization plan to take over government offices. Within hours it will be decided.
event_desc.deu_mr_pact_offer: Moscow has proposed a non-aggression treaty first. The Soviet foreign commissar also wants to discuss a secret protocol dividing Eastern Europe into spheres of interest. Signing would leave Germany free to face the West without worrying about the East.
event_desc.deu_occupy_hungary: Our envoys report that Budapest is seeking a separate peace while the Red Army nears the Carpathians. The Regent has been summoned to talks in Austria; while he is away, our divisions can secure Hungary and install a reliable government.
event_desc.deu_olympics: The XI Olympic Games open in Berlin. The government has built a new stadium and dressed the streets for foreign visitors. For two weeks the eyes of the world are on Germany, and the regime means to show it a calm and orderly country.
event_desc.deu_poland: German forces crossed the border into Poland at dawn. Panzer divisions and dive bombers lead the way while the Polish army fights back all along the frontier. The question now is whether Poland's allies will keep their word.
event_desc.deu_renounce_polish_pact: Poland has flatly refused the demands over Danzig and the Corridor. Berlin holds that the 1934 German–Polish declaration of non-aggression no longer means anything and prepares to announce in the Reichstag that it is void.
event_desc.deu_rhineland_bluff: France has begun to mobilize in answer to the march into the Rhineland. The generals warn that the few battalions on the border cannot stop the French army. Pulling back costs face; standing firm means risking war.
event_desc.deu_september_coup: Officers around General Ludwig Beck have finally moved. Troops of the Berlin military district are heading for the government quarter, but no one knows how the police and the party will respond. The officers mean to arrest the regime's leaders and form a provisional government.
event_desc.deu_social_republic: German paratroopers have freed Mussolini from his mountain prison. He is ready to head a fascist government in the north of Italy, seated at Salò on Lake Garda, that would keep the occupied provinces at our side.
event_desc.deu_sudeten_refused: Czechoslovakia refuses to give up the Sudetenland. Its border fortifications are strong, and no one knows what the Western powers will do. Choosing war may mean a wider conflict; stepping back costs the regime face.
event_desc.deu_tripartite_signing: Germany has sent the text of a treaty to be signed together in Berlin. The three powers recognize each other's new order in Europe and East Asia and pledge to stand together if any of them is attacked by a power not yet in the war.
event_desc.deu_vienna_award_1: After Munich, Hungary asks for arbitration to recover the Hungarian-populated districts of southern Czechoslovakia. The German and Italian foreign ministers offer to draw a new border in Vienna. If the award goes ahead, southern Slovakia passes to Hungary.
event_desc.deu_vienna_award_2: With Romania having yielded Bessarabia to the Soviets, Hungary demands Transylvania and threatens war. Needing Romania's oil safe, Germany joins Italy in arbitrating once more to draw a line between the two.
event_desc.dnk_german_treaty: Berlin offers Copenhagen a treaty of non-aggression. Sweden and Norway have declined the same offer, but Denmark shares a land border with Germany and has almost no army to defend it. Signing would calm relations with Berlin but displease London.
event_desc.esp_civil_war: Army garrisons in Morocco and across the mainland have risen against the Republic. Where the rising failed, workers' militias hold the streets; where it succeeded, the generals rule. Spain is split in two. Foreign governments weigh which side to help.
event_desc.esp_civil_war_ends: The last resistance of the other side has collapsed and the guns have fallen silent across Spain. The victors now govern the whole country and must rebuild the towns, railways and fields the war has ruined.
event_desc.esp_civil_war_won: The other side has collapsed and the guns have fallen silent across Spain. The country is exhausted and divided, but the war that split it in two is over. Towns lie in ruins and many thousands have fled across the border.
event_desc.esr_international_brigades: Volunteers from dozens of countries are arriving at Albacete to fight for the Republic. Many have never held a rifle, but they come with conviction, and the government has agreed to organise them into brigades of their own.
event_desc.esr_popular_front: The left-wing Popular Front has narrowly won the February general election. A Republican government takes office amid strikes, land seizures and street fighting, while army officers and the right talk openly of a rising. The country is pulling apart.
event_desc.eth_restoration: British and Commonwealth troops, with Ethiopian patriot fighters, have driven the Italians from Addis Ababa. Emperor Haile Selassie, in exile since 1936, is ready to enter his capital five years to the day after the Italians took it.
event_desc.fin_moscow_armistice: The Soviet summer offensive has broken our lines on the Karelian Isthmus. Moscow's terms: the 1940 border, Petsamo, a lease on the Porkkala peninsula, reparations, and the removal of German troops from Finnish soil, by force if need be.
event_desc.fin_moscow_peace: Moscow offers peace at a heavy price: the whole Karelian Isthmus with Viipuri, the shores of Lake Ladoga and land in the far north. The army can hold for weeks more, not months, and Western help has not arrived.
event_desc.fin_soviet_demands: Moscow demands that we move the border on the Karelian Isthmus back from Leningrad, hand over islands in the Gulf of Finland and lease the port of Hanko as a naval base. Our delegates have come home to consult the government. Most Finns oppose any concession.
event_desc.fin_winter_war_flag: Soviet troops have crossed the Finnish border and bombers have struck Helsinki. Finland's small army digs in on the Karelian Isthmus and in the frozen forests to the north. Most observers expect the fight to last only weeks.
event_desc.fra_daladier: The second Blum cabinet has fallen after less than a month. Édouard Daladier, the Radical minister of war, forms a government that leans to the centre and promises to put rearmament before reform. Parliament prepares to let him govern by decree.
event_desc.fra_election_1936: France goes to the polls deeply divided. The Popular Front of Radicals, Socialists and Communists promises bread, peace and freedom; the parties of the right warn of disorder and strikes. The second round will decide who governs.
event_desc.fra_free_french_africa: Governor Félix Éboué announces that Chad stands with Free France. Within days Cameroon and the French Congo follow, giving General de Gaulle land of his own, a capital at Brazzaville and a road across Africa.
event_desc.fra_hatay_cession: Ankara asks France to let the Sanjak of Alexandretta, now the State of Hatay, join Turkey. Syrian nationalists will call it a betrayal of the mandate, but Turkish goodwill could matter greatly in the Mediterranean if war comes.
event_desc.fra_joins_guarantee: London has pledged to defend an eastern European state against aggression and asks Paris to join the guarantee. France already has treaties of its own in the east; standing beside Britain would show that the two democracies act as one.
event_desc.fra_paris_uprising: Allied armies are closing on the capital. The police, the railwaymen and the resistance groups of Paris seize public buildings and put up barricades against the German garrison.
event_desc.fra_regime_crisis: The entry of the leagues into government has split the country. Strikes and street demonstrations spread, and both the ministers and the parties of the left claim to be defending France.
event_desc.fra_rhineland_response: German battalions have marched into the demilitarised Rhineland, tearing up the Locarno treaty. The General Staff says any answer means general mobilisation weeks before an election, and London urges restraint. Every day of hesitation makes the new line harder to undo.
event_desc.fra_wartime_unity: A year of war has quieted the quarrels of the Third Republic. Parties that fought each other in the streets in 1934 now sit together, and strikes have given way to long shifts in the arms factories. At last France fights the war with one voice.
event_desc.gbr_abdication: Edward VIII insists on marrying Wallis Simpson, who has been divorced twice. The Prime Minister and the Dominion governments refuse to accept her as Queen. Either the King goes or the government does.
event_desc.gbr_abdication_settled: The Duke of York has become King George VI. Shy and troubled by a stammer, he reassures the country with his steady manner. The crisis has passed, and Parliament and Palace return to their normal business.
event_desc.gbr_anglo_soviet_agreement: Three weeks after Germany invaded the Soviet Union, Britain and the USSR sign an agreement in Moscow. Each promises to help the other in the war against Germany and never to make a separate peace.
event_desc.gbr_attlee_government: Labour leader Clement Attlee is now at the head of the government. Trade union leaders take ministerial posts, and the government promises to tackle unemployment and rearmament together through planning.
event_desc.gbr_chamberlain: Stanley Baldwin retires after the coronation. The Chancellor of the Exchequer, Neville Chamberlain, becomes Conservative leader and Prime Minister, convinced that patient negotiation can keep the peace in Europe.
event_desc.gbr_churchill: Disappointed with the conduct of the war, the House of Commons turns on the government. Labour refuses to serve under Chamberlain, so he resigns, and Winston Churchill forms a government of all parties.
event_desc.gbr_eden_resigns: Foreign Secretary Anthony Eden resigns after clashing with the Prime Minister over talks with Italy. Chamberlain wants to deal with Mussolini now; Eden wants concessions from Rome first. Lord Halifax takes over the Foreign Office.
event_desc.gbr_eden_returns: Lord Halifax leaves for Washington as ambassador. Anthony Eden returns to the Foreign Office, where wartime diplomacy now means keeping the Americans and the Soviets close.
event_desc.gbr_election_1945: With the war in Europe over, the coalition breaks up and the first general election in ten years is held. The count waited three weeks for the servicemen's votes. The country has chosen between the leader who won the war and a promise to rebuild.
event_desc.gbr_habbaniya: Iraqi troops have taken the heights above our air base at Habbaniya and threaten the road to the Gulf oil fields. The government in Baghdad will not pull them back. Under the 1930 treaty we have the right to move troops through Iraq.
event_desc.gbr_levant_campaign: German aircraft bound for Iraq have refuelled on Vichy airfields in Syria. The Levant could become an Axis foothold beside Suez. Our forces in Palestine, with the Free French, are ready to march on Damascus and Beirut.
event_desc.gbr_mers_el_kebir: A large part of the French battle fleet lies at Mers-el-Kébir near Oran, and Britain cannot risk those ships passing to Germany. A British squadron arrives off the harbour with terms: sail with us, sail to a distant port under guard, or scuttle.
event_desc.gbr_new_king: On 20 January 1936 King George V dies at Sandringham, and the Prince of Wales succeeds him as Edward VIII. The new King is popular, but his attachment to an American divorcée already worries the Cabinet.
event_desc.gbr_non_intervention_committee: Delegates of twenty-seven governments meet in London and agree that no arms will reach either side in Spain. Germany, Italy and the Soviet Union have signed too, and few expect them to keep their word. Staying out may spare Europe a wider war, or simply leave the Republic alone.
event_desc.gbr_prague_shock: German troops have entered Prague, less than six months after the promises made at Munich. In a speech in Birmingham the Prime Minister asks whether this is the last attack on a small state, and public opinion decides that the time for concessions is over.
event_desc.gbr_soviet_alliance_offer: Having turned Germany away, the Soviet government offers Britain and France a treaty of mutual assistance. With it Germany would face enemies in both east and west, but many in London still distrust the Bolsheviks.
event_desc.gbr_soviet_overture: The British ambassador brings the Kremlin a draft pact: neither country will attack the other, and both will stand against aggression. If they are at war, a clause also lets each side's forces cross the other's territory.
event_desc.gen_call_to_arms: A member of our faction has gone to war and asks us to fight at its side. Answering the call makes its enemy our enemy. Refusing would keep us out of the war but cost us trust within the alliance.
event_desc.gen_coup_done: Overnight, army units and their political allies seized the ministries and the radio station in the capital. The old government has fallen, and the new one has announced its rule on the radio. Rumours in the streets say a foreign power helped.
event_desc.gen_diplo_access: A government asks that its troops be allowed to cross our territory. If we agree, its armies may move through and stay on our soil. We may withdraw permission whenever we wish.
event_desc.gen_diplo_faction_invite: The leader of a faction has invited us to become a member. Members fight together and defend one another. If the faction is at war, we will be at war with its enemies at once.
event_desc.gen_diplo_faction_request: A government has asked to join our faction. Accepting means its borders become a front we must help to hold. A new member takes part in every war the faction fights.
event_desc.gen_diplo_lend_lease: A government asks us to send equipment from our stockpiles every month, shipped at our expense. The supplies would strengthen a useful friend but leave less for our own divisions.
event_desc.gen_diplo_nap: A government proposes a treaty under which neither side will attack the other. While it lasts, neither may justify a war against the other or declare one. Breaking it later would take time and cost us dearly.
event_desc.gen_election: The polls have closed and every ballot box has been opened. The voters decide who should lead parliament, but how the result is received is for the present government to settle. The whole country is watching.
event_desc.gen_exile_formed: The country's armies have been defeated and its land is occupied, but its government has escaped abroad. From an allied capital it keeps its remaining forces in the war and speaks for the occupied people.
event_desc.gen_government_shift: A political movement has won over most of the nation and now speaks for the majority. Crowds and newspapers demand that the cabinet step down and hand over power. The government cannot put off its answer for long.
event_desc.gen_guarantee_called: A country whose independence we guaranteed has been attacked. Keeping our word means war with the aggressor. Standing aside would spare us the fighting, but our promises would carry little weight again.
event_desc.gen_justified_against: Reports say a foreign government has begun building a case for war against us. The newspapers write daily of troop movements and hostile speeches beyond the border. Now is the time to strengthen our defences.
event_desc.gen_munich_conference: Germany demands the Sudetenland and threatens war if it is refused. The leaders of the great powers meet in Munich to settle Czechoslovakia's frontier, with no Czechoslovak at the table. Our word will decide whether Prague is told to yield or is defended.
event_desc.gen_peace_conference: The guns have fallen silent and the victors are gathering to decide the fate of the defeated. Each will press its claims in turn; the larger its part in the victory, the more it can ask for.
event_desc.gen_peace_movement: As the war drags on, rallies and petitions for peace appear across the country. More deputies speak openly of a negotiated end. The government must let the movement be heard or answer it with propaganda.
event_desc.gen_regime_crisis: For more than a month a movement outside the government has held the support of most of the people. Strikes and demonstrations go on, and doubts are spreading among officers and officials. The government must step aside or hold on by force.
event_desc.gen_strike: Workers angered by low wages and rising prices have laid down their tools. Factories stand idle, and the strike is spreading to the docks and railways. The government can bear the lost output or end the strike with concessions.
event_desc.gen_subject_upgrade: A government under our protection asks to manage more of its own affairs. Granting it would loosen our hold but earn goodwill; refusing would keep it close and may push it toward a break.
event_desc.gen_unrest: Distrust of the government has grown, and protests and clashes break out in several cities. Reports say the police alone can no longer keep order. We must wait for calm or declare martial law.
event_desc.gen_uprising: Armed fighters have driven the occupying garrison out of a region and raised their own flag over its town halls. Whether they can hold it depends on how quickly help arrives.
event_desc.gen_volunteers_arrive: A friendly government has sent volunteers to fight at our side. They come with their own officers and equipment and stay under their own command, but they will fight our enemies.
event_desc.gen_war_weariness: Lost provinces and ever longer casualty lists weigh on the people. More men dodge the draft, and the newspapers have grown gloomy. The government can let morale sag or spend heavily to lift it.
event_desc.hun_horthy_armistice: The Red Army stands on the Great Hungarian Plain. The Regent's envoys in Moscow have agreed preliminary armistice terms, and he is ready to announce on the radio that Hungary is leaving the war. Berlin will not stand by.
event_desc.irn_armistice: British troops advance from Iraq and the Gulf, Soviet columns from the Caucasus, and our army cannot hold either front. The two powers demand a supply route to the Soviet Union and the expulsion of German nationals. The Shah's government can stop the fighting today.
event_desc.irn_new_shah: Reza Shah has abdicated as Soviet troops approach Tehran and will leave the country. His son Mohammad Reza takes the oath before the Majlis and promises to rule as a constitutional monarch.
event_desc.irq_armistice: British columns are closing on Baghdad and German air support has come too late. The leaders of the coup are fleeing to Iran. Officers loyal to the regent are ready to sign an armistice and bring back the old government.
event_desc.irq_golden_square: Four army colonels known as the Golden Square have surrounded the palace in Baghdad. The regent has fled, and the officers want a National Defence Government that would end British influence and look to the Axis for help.
event_desc.isl_british_occupation: British warships have landed troops at Reykjavík without asking. London says it must keep Iceland out of German hands now that Denmark is occupied, and promises to leave when the war ends. We have no army to resist them.
event_desc.isl_us_garrison: Washington offers to take over the defence of Iceland from the British, and our government has invited it. American marines will garrison the island while the British troops leave for other fronts.
event_desc.ita_addis_ababa: Italian columns have entered Addis Ababa and the Emperor has left for exile. Rome is ready to proclaim the King of Italy Emperor of Ethiopia and join the country to its East African possessions, whatever the League decides.
event_desc.ita_albania: Italian troops have landed at Durrës and other Albanian ports. King Zog has fled across the border, and Rome prepares to offer the Albanian crown to the King of Italy. The small kingdom's army cannot hold out for long.
event_desc.ita_alpine_armistice: France has laid down its arms, and its delegates have signed a separate armistice with Italy at Villa Incisa near Rome. Italy keeps the ground its troops hold beyond the Alps, and a demilitarised strip is drawn along the frontier.
event_desc.ita_anti_comintern: Berlin and Tokyo invite Rome to join their pact against the Communist International. Membership costs little on paper, but it would bind Italy publicly to Germany and Japan. London and Paris are watching Rome's choice.
event_desc.ita_armistice: The new government has secretly signed an armistice with the Allies at Cassibile in Sicily. Announcing it takes Italy out of the war and out of the Axis at once, while German divisions are already in the north.
event_desc.ita_cobelligerence: From Brindisi, where the King and the government have taken refuge, Italy declares war on Germany. The Allies accept it as a co-belligerent, not as an ally, and Italian units now fight beside the Allied armies moving up the peninsula.
event_desc.ita_grand_council: With the war going badly, the Fascist Grand Council has met for the first time since 1939. After ten hours of debate it passed Dino Grandi's motion asking the King to take back supreme command. The next day the King dismissed Mussolini, had him arrested and gave the government to a marshal.
event_desc.ita_leaves_league: The Fascist Grand Council has decided that Italy will leave the League of Nations, which condemned the war in Ethiopia. The announcement from a balcony in Rome draws cheers at home and cold silence in London and Paris. Rome is no longer bound by anything Geneva decides.
event_desc.ita_mussolini_restrained: Monarchists, generals and a group of moderate Fascists have agreed to act together in the Grand Council. If the vote goes their way, the King will give the government to a marshal; if it fails, Mussolini will settle scores.
event_desc.ita_pact_of_steel: Berlin proposes a full military alliance: each will come to the other's aid in any war, defensive or not. The foreign ministry warns that Italy will not be ready for a great war before 1943.
event_desc.ita_rome_berlin_axis: Italy's foreign minister has signed a protocol in Berlin settling the two governments' differences over Austria, Spain and Ethiopia. Rome can speak of an axis around which Europe will turn, or keep Berlin at arm's length.
event_desc.ita_sanctions_lifted: With Ethiopia in Italian hands, the League of Nations has ended its economic sanctions. They never covered oil and many members ignored them; their end is a quiet admission that collective security has failed.
event_desc.jpn_anti_comintern: Berlin proposes a pact against the Communist International, with a secret annex promising that neither side will help the Soviet Union against the other. The army welcomes it; the navy and the court fear it ties Japan to Germany's quarrels.
event_desc.jpn_burma_state: Under Japanese military rule, Burma's independence preparatory committee has drafted a constitution. Ending military rule and proclaiming an independent State of Burma should win Burmese cooperation. The new state, however, must ally with Japan and declare war on Britain and America.
event_desc.jpn_february_incident: Young army officers have seized the centre of Tokyo and killed senior statesmen, demanding a 'Shōwa Restoration' under direct imperial rule. The throne wants the revolt crushed; the army command is split over how far to meet the rebels.
event_desc.jpn_hull_note: In Washington the Secretary of State has handed the Japanese envoys a note. It asks Japan to withdraw all its forces from China and Indochina and to join a multilateral non-aggression pact. The cabinet reads it as an ultimatum in all but name. The navy's preparations are already complete.
event_desc.jpn_imperial_rule_assistance: The prime minister has gathered the dissolved political parties into a single Imperial Rule Assistance Association. The Diet remains, but every organisation from labour to women's groups is to be folded into one national movement. The cabinet calls it the New Order.
event_desc.jpn_marco_polo_bridge: A night clash between Japanese and Chinese troops near the Marco Polo Bridge outside Beiping has grown into open fighting. Neither government backs down, and the skirmish becomes a full war between Japan and China. Within weeks the front spreads across northern China.
event_desc.jpn_nanjing_government: Nationalist figures who broke with Chongqing propose a new National Government in Nanjing, merging the client regimes Japan set up in northern and central China. It can only rest on Japanese recognition and Japanese garrisons. Chongqing calls it a puppet and vows to fight on.
event_desc.jpn_philippine_republic: In Manila the Preparatory Commission for Philippine Independence has drafted a constitution. If Japan grants independence, military rule ends and a republic under a Filipino president takes its place. The Commonwealth government in exile in Washington does not recognise it.
event_desc.jpn_potsdam_declaration: From Potsdam, the United States, Britain and China have called on Japan to surrender unconditionally. The alternative, they warn, is prompt and utter destruction. The cabinet and the military chiefs are divided over how to answer.
event_desc.jpn_south_indochina: Japan has sent a second demand. This time it wants the airfields and ports of southern Indochina, Saigon among them, and the right to station troops there. With the homeland occupied, there is no strength to resist. Washington is watching and weighing its answer.
event_desc.jpn_soviet_neutrality: Moscow offers a pact of neutrality: each side will stay out of any war the other fights. It would secure the northern frontier while the army is tied down in China and the navy looks south. The pact would run for five years.
event_desc.jpn_surrender_decision: The Soviet Union has declared war and driven into Manchuria, and the cities of the home islands are being destroyed from the air. The Supreme War Council is split three against three over accepting the Potsdam terms. An imperial conference must make the final decision.
event_desc.jpn_surrender_effect: Through neutral governments, Japan has told the Allies it accepts the Potsdam Declaration, and the surrender has been announced to the nation by radio. The armed forces have been ordered to cease fire. The war in Asia and the Pacific is drawing to an end.
event_desc.ltu_memel_ultimatum: Berlin demands the Memel Territory, detached from Germany after the war and held by Lithuania since 1923, and hints that any delay will be settled by force. Britain and France have just stood aside over Prague.
event_desc.phl_osmena_succeeds: President Quezon has died at Saranac Lake, New York, after a long illness. Vice President Sergio Osmeña takes the oath of office in Washington and pledges to bring the Commonwealth government home to Manila.
event_desc.pol_danzig_bargain: Berlin offers Warsaw a partnership: if Danzig returns to Germany and a German road crosses the corridor, Germany will guarantee Poland's frontiers and share its gains in the east. The offer comes with a smile and an army behind it.
event_desc.pol_danzig_demand: Germany demands the Free City of Danzig and an extraterritorial road and railway across the Polish corridor to East Prussia. Warsaw sees the corridor as its outlet to the sea, and the army has begun calling up reservists.
event_desc.pol_warsaw_uprising: Soviet tanks are reported on the eastern approaches to Warsaw. The commander of the Home Army in the city asks our authorisation to rise against the German garrison and free the capital before the Red Army arrives.
event_desc.potsdam_conference: At Cecilienhof, outside ruined Berlin, the victorious powers fix Germany's eastern border on the Oder and the Neisse and divide East Prussia. Before they part, they will call on Japan to surrender.
event_desc.rou_antonescu: Blamed for the summer's losses of territory, King Carol II has abdicated in favour of his son Michael. The general he named prime minister now rules with full powers as Conducător of the state, backed by the Iron Guard. Parliament stays dissolved.
event_desc.rou_august_coup: Soviet armies have broken through in Moldavia. The young King and the opposition parties are ready to arrest the head of government at the palace, announce an armistice with the Allies on the radio and turn the army against Germany.
event_desc.rou_bessarabia_ultimatum: Moscow demands Bessarabia and northern Bukovina, with twenty-four hours to answer and four days to evacuate. Berlin advises Bucharest to give way, and no ally is ready to help. If we refuse, Soviet troops will cross the Dniester.
event_desc.rou_dobruja: Sofia asks for the return of Southern Dobruja, taken from Bulgaria after the Balkan wars. Berlin backs the claim, and after this summer's losses Bucharest has neither the will nor the friends to refuse. The agreement is to be signed at Craiova.
event_desc.rou_vienna_award_notice: Summoned to Vienna, our foreign minister has been handed a map: northern Transylvania, with Cluj and Oradea, goes to Hungary. Germany and Italy will guarantee what is left of Romania if we accept. At home, the news is met with fury.
event_desc.sun_annex_east_poland: Assemblies convened in the occupied Polish east have asked to join the Ukrainian and Belorussian Soviet republics. The Supreme Soviet can accept the request and make the border final.
event_desc.sun_barbarossa: At dawn, German armies cross the border along its whole length, from the Baltic to the Black Sea. Airfields are bombed before the planes can take off, and whole armies are cut off within days. Molotov speaks to the country by radio: "Our cause is just."
event_desc.sun_blyukher_arrest: Marshal Vasily Blyukher, a hero of the Civil War who had led the army in the Far East since 1929, is relieved after the fighting at Lake Khasan and arrested on 22 October. He dies in custody the following month.
event_desc.sun_bukharin_arrest: At the February–March plenum of the Central Committee, Nikolai Bukharin and Alexei Rykov are expelled from the party and arrested on 27 February. Bukharin edited Izvestia from 1934; Rykov had headed the government until 1930.
event_desc.sun_first_moscow_trial: In Moscow, Grigory Zinoviev, Lev Kamenev and fourteen other defendants stand trial for an alleged plot against the party leadership. The case rests on their own confessions, printed in full in every newspaper. The court convicts all sixteen, and a wave of arrests follows.
event_desc.sun_japan_pact_lapses: Months after the notice, Moscow no longer treats the neutrality pact with Japan as binding. Since the spring, troops and equipment have rolled east along the Trans-Siberian without pause. The armies gathered in the Far East wait for their orders.
event_desc.sun_khalkhin_gol: Mongolian and Japanese-Manchukuo forces clash over the border along the Khalkhin Gol river. Under the 1936 protocol, Soviet troops move in to support Mongolia, and by late summer the skirmishes have grown into a full-scale battle.
event_desc.sun_lake_khasan: Japanese troops seize the hills west of Lake Khasan, on the border between the Soviet Union and Manchukuo. The Red Army retakes them after two weeks of hard fighting, and the ceasefire of 11 August leaves the border where Moscow drew it.
event_desc.sun_litvinov_dismissed: Maxim Litvinov, the face of collective security for nearly nine years, is removed as People's Commissar for Foreign Affairs. Premier Vyacheslav Molotov takes the post himself. In Berlin the change is read as a signal.
event_desc.sun_military_trial: A special session of the Supreme Court tries Marshal Mikhail Tukhachevsky, army commanders Iona Yakir and Ieronim Uborevich and five other senior officers for treason behind closed doors. The hearing lasts a single day, and all eight are convicted. Arrests spread through the officer corps.
event_desc.sun_mr_pact_offer: The German Foreign Minister has arrived in Moscow with an offer: a ten-year non-aggression pact and a secret protocol dividing Eastern Europe into spheres of interest. Britain and France have offered nothing comparable. Signing would keep the Soviet Union out of the coming war, at least for now.
event_desc.sun_poland: Soviet troops cross the Polish border from the east, declaring that the Polish state has ceased to exist. Moscow presents the move as protecting the Ukrainians and Belarusians who live beyond the border. The two invading armies meet along the line drawn in the secret protocol.
event_desc.sun_renounce_japan_pact: Foreign Commissar Molotov receives the Japanese ambassador and reads a statement: Japan, Germany's ally, is helping Germany in its war against the USSR, so the neutrality pact cannot be extended. Tokyo is left to guess at Moscow's intentions.
event_desc.sun_rokossovsky_arrest: Konstantin Rokossovsky, a cavalry commander with a distinguished record since the Civil War, is arrested on charges of spying for Poland and Japan. He will spend the next two and a half years in prison under investigation.
event_desc.sun_rokossovsky_release: After two and a half years under investigation, Konstantin Rokossovsky is released on 22 March 1940 and restored to his rank. He returns to command.
event_desc.sun_shaposhnikov_returns: With the front giving way, Marshal Boris Shaposhnikov is recalled to head the General Staff in place of Georgy Zhukov. He had held the same post from 1937 to 1940. His calm and methodical staff work is needed more than ever.
event_desc.sun_shaposhnikov_steps_down: In failing health, Marshal Shaposhnikov leaves the post of Chief of the General Staff. His deputy, Aleksandr Vasilevsky, head of operations since August 1941, carries on the work and is confirmed in the post in June.
event_desc.sun_third_moscow_trial: Nikolai Bukharin, Alexei Rykov and nineteen other former leaders stand trial in Moscow for treason and sabotage. Foreign diplomats and journalists watch from the gallery as the defendants confess. On 13 March the court convicts all twenty-one.
event_desc.sun_tupolev_arrest: Aircraft designer Andrei Tupolev is arrested along with several of his engineers, among them Vladimir Petlyakov. From 1939 they design aircraft in a design bureau set up inside a prison.
event_desc.sun_tupolev_released: Andrei Tupolev and many of his engineers are released early to build aircraft for the war. The Tu-2 bomber they designed in prison is readied for production. Tupolev will not be fully rehabilitated until 1955.
event_desc.sun_vilnius_to_lithuania: Our troops hold Vilnius, which Lithuania has claimed as its capital since 1920. A mutual assistance treaty would hand the city to the government in Kaunas in return for Soviet garrisons on Lithuanian soil.
event_desc.sun_yegorov_replaced: Marshal Alexander Yegorov hands the General Staff over to Boris Shaposhnikov and becomes First Deputy People's Commissar of Defense. It is one move in a sweeping reshuffle of the high command that spring.
event_desc.svk_independence: With Bohemia and Moravia in our hands, Slovak politicians in Bratislava are ready to declare a state of their own under our protection. A separate Slovakia would guard our flank at little cost; ruling it directly would keep the land in our own hands.
event_desc.svk_national_uprising: Army units and partisans in the central Slovak mountains have risen against the government and its German protectors, with Banská Bystrica as their centre. German divisions are moving in to put the rising down and occupy the region.
event_desc.tehran_conference: For the first time the leaders of the Soviet Union, the United States and the United Kingdom sit at one table, at the Soviet embassy in Tehran. They agree that a second front will open in France in the spring of 1944.
event_desc.tha_border_war: With France defeated, crowds in Bangkok demand the return of the lands west of the Mekong that Siam ceded to French Indochina in 1904 and 1907. Border clashes have already begun, and the government must choose between war and patience.
event_desc.tha_tokyo_peace: Japan has offered to mediate the border war with Siam and expects an answer. Its terms would cede the lands west of the Mekong and around Battambang to Siam. Refusing would mean fighting on alone.
event_desc.tur_ataturk_dies: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, founder of the Republic, has died in Istanbul. The Grand National Assembly turns to İsmet İnönü, his long-serving prime minister and comrade from the War of Independence. The country goes into deep mourning.
event_desc.usa_atlantic_charter: Meeting aboard warships off Newfoundland, the President and the British Prime Minister have set out common aims for the world after the war: no territorial gains, self-determination, open trade and freedom from fear and want.
event_desc.usa_destroyers_for_bases: London asks for fifty old American destroyers to guard its convoys. In return Britain offers ninety-nine-year leases on bases from Newfoundland to British Guiana. The deal would bypass Congress and stretch neutrality to its limit.
event_desc.usa_election_1936: Americans choose between Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal and the Republican Alf Landon, who promises to balance the budget. Relief programmes, union rights and Social Security are on the ballot as much as the man in the White House.
event_desc.usa_election_1940: With war in Europe, Roosevelt breaks tradition and runs for a third term against Wendell Willkie. Both men promise to help Britain while keeping America out of the fighting; the voters must decide whom they trust in a crisis.
event_desc.usa_election_1944: For the first time since 1864 Americans vote in the middle of a great war. A visibly tired Roosevelt faces Thomas E. Dewey; his running mate this time is Senator Harry S. Truman of Missouri.
event_desc.usa_isolation_ends: Events abroad have overwhelmed the case for staying out. With the world at war, Congress and the public accept that the United States can no longer stand apart from it. The neutrality laws lose their force.
event_desc.usa_isolation_strained: As crisis follows crisis abroad, more Americans ask whether the oceans still keep the country safe. The neutrality laws stay on the books, but Congress has begun to argue over how far they should bind the President.
event_desc.usa_lend_lease_act: Congress has passed An Act to Promote the Defense of the United States. The President may now lend or lease war materials to any country whose defence he judges vital to America, and Britain's dollar shortage no longer limits its orders.
event_desc.usa_pearl_harbor: Japanese carrier aircraft have struck the Pacific Fleet at Pearl Harbor while Japanese forces attack across the Pacific. The President asks Congress to recognise that a state of war exists, and the isolationists fall silent.
event_desc.usa_quarantine_speech: In Chicago the President likens the spread of lawlessness in the world to an epidemic and calls on peace-loving nations to quarantine the aggressors. The press is divided, and isolationists in Congress are furious. No measures have yet been named.
event_desc.usa_recession_1937: Share prices have plunged and factory output is falling fast after Washington cut spending to balance the budget. Advisers urge the President to open the public purse again; the Treasury warns that the deficits will never end.
event_desc.usa_roosevelt_dies: Franklin D. Roosevelt has died at Warm Springs, Georgia, before the war's end. Vice President Harry S. Truman, little known abroad and barely briefed on the war, takes the oath of office.
event_desc.usa_united_nations: Representatives of the nations at war with the Axis gather in Washington to sign a joint declaration: each pledges its full resources to the common struggle and promises not to make a separate peace. It is the first document to use the name 'United Nations'.
event_desc.vic_dakar: A British and Free French squadron appears off Dakar and calls on the colony to join General de Gaulle. The battleship in the harbour and the coastal batteries stand ready, and the governor-general must choose between the guns and the envoys.
event_desc.vic_fleet_ultimatum: The British admiral gives our squadron a few hours: sail to a British port or to the West Indies under guard, or be sunk where it lies. Yet the armistice forbids us to hand over a single ship.
event_desc.vic_full_powers: Meeting in the casino theatre at Vichy, deputies and senators vote 569 to 80 to grant full powers to write a new constitution. The next day the President of the Council becomes Head of the French State, and the Third Republic is over.
event_desc.vic_head_of_government: Under German pressure, a constitutional act creates the post of head of government. A minister dismissed at the end of 1940 returns to run domestic and foreign policy, while the head of state keeps his title.
event_desc.vic_japanese_demand: Japan demands airfields, garrisons and the right to move troops through northern Indochina, to cut the railway that supplies China. The governor-general has few soldiers and can expect no help from France.
event_desc.vic_levant_armistice: After five weeks of fighting, Damascus has fallen and British, Australian, Indian and Free French columns stand before Beirut. The high commissioner asks for terms: at Acre the Levant is handed over, and its garrison may sail home to France.
event_desc.vic_madagascar_armistice: Six months after British troops landed at Diego-Suarez, the last Vichy garrison in the south of the island has nowhere left to fall back to. The governor-general signs an armistice.
event_desc.vic_torch: American and British troops have landed at Casablanca, Oran and Algiers. After two days of fighting, the senior Vichy commanders in Algiers must decide whether to order a ceasefire or keep fighting the landings.
event_desc.vic_toulon: German troops are racing into the naval base at Toulon to seize the fleet. The admirals have standing orders that no ship may fall into foreign hands, and the scuttling charges are already in place.
event_desc.yalta_conference: The three Allied leaders meet at the Livadia Palace in the Crimea. They settle the zones of occupation in Germany, and the Soviet Union promises to enter the war against Japan within three months of Germany's defeat.
event_desc.yug_belgrade_coup: Air force officers move against the government that signed the pact. Crowds fill the streets of Belgrade, and the conspirators want to declare the seventeen-year-old Peter II of age and end the regency. Berlin will treat it as a betrayal.
event_desc.yug_occupation_partition: With the Yugoslav government in exile, the occupying powers draw their lines. We take northern Slovenia; Italy takes Ljubljana and the Dalmatian coast; Hungary takes Bačka and Baranja; Bulgaria takes Vardar Macedonia. What remains of Serbia stays under our military administration.
event_desc.yug_rump_serbia: The peace has left us only the Serbian heartland, bound to Germany. The name of a kingdom of the South Slavs no longer fits a state that rules from Belgrade alone, and the cabinet proposes to call the country Serbia.
event_desc.yug_tripartite: Berlin presses Belgrade to join the Tripartite Pact. Every neighbour but Greece has already signed, and the Regent has been promised that no Axis troops will cross Yugoslav soil. Many officers and Serbian politicians are bitterly opposed.
event_desc.zaf_parliament_vote: Britain's declaration of war on Germany splits the South African parliament. The Prime Minister wants to stay neutral; his deputy, Jan Smuts, wants to fight beside Britain. The vote will decide the country's course.
